surfaces.name: Explicitly admitted Haxe-to-C compiler slices
protectedClaims: Only capability-manifest slices with real typed-Haxe lowering, strict C build, and runtime evidence are admitted.
Official Haxe qualification applies only to explicitly mapped admitted scope.
oracles: Pinned Haxe Eval differential traces for shared Haxe semantics
Manually reviewed HxcIR and generated-C expectations paired with strict native execution

evidence.proves: One ordinary Haxe literal-output tracer crosses haxe.c, strict C11, and a native runtime observer.
evidence.doesNotProve: General Haxe lowering, general String support, platform support, or a stable public ABI.

evidence.proves: The bounded String suite proves fresh decoded enum carriers and retained String payload aliases with Eval, strict native execution, and sanitizer observers; the enum suite separately proves the synchronous String constructor-callback adapter.
evidence.doesNotProve: Other managed or recursive enum-constructor callback payloads, full standard-library String behavior, or general Haxe lowering.

evidence.proves: The bounded Bytes suite proves borrowed and fresh Bytes values cross compiler-generated switch and conditional joins, while an explicit nullable local preserves absent, present-empty, and present-non-empty states through checked unwrap, replacement, and cleanup, using Eval, validated HxcIR, strict native execution, and sanitizer observers.
evidence.doesNotProve: Nullable Bytes parameters, returns, fields, or other erased-null storage shapes; full standard-library Bytes behavior; a public ABI; platform qualification; or general Haxe lowering.

evidence.proves: One bounded ordinary-Haxe JSON codec crosses the admitted enum, class, Array, Bytes, and String slices through strict generated C.
evidence.doesNotProve: General Haxe lowering, a general JSON library, runtime pack loading, public ABI stability, or platform qualification.

evidence.proves: One typed package-role and receipt model crosses bounded JSON, the confined directory source, haxe.c, strict native C, and every declared first-adventure payload.
evidence.doesNotProve: General Haxe lowering, ZIP transport, arbitrary mod activation, dependency resolution, public ABI stability, or platform qualification.

evidence.proves: One frozen independently produced stored ZIP crosses the Haxe-authored bounded parser, the transport-neutral package verifier, haxe.c, strict native C, and a real observer with 36 fail-closed archive mutations.
evidence.doesNotProve: Current-package directory parity, general Haxe lowering, general haxe.zip support, Deflate, deterministic export, complete asset handoff, arbitrary mod activation, public ABI stability, or platform qualification.

evidence.proves: One admitted Haxe slice verifies a complete campaign/level/pack/localization/asset package, writes a deterministic stored ZIP, reopens it through the bounded reader, and preserves the exact package identity through strict native C.
evidence.doesNotProve: General Haxe lowering, general haxe.zip support, Deflate, arbitrary package compatibility, mod installation or activation, public ABI stability, or platform qualification.

evidence.proves: The checked-in content and UI bytes cross the package store, bounded JSON codec, exact target-owned schemas, immutable registry/catalog, strict generated C, and a real runtime observer.
evidence.doesNotProve: General Haxe lowering, arbitrary pack compatibility, publication into the running game, public ABI stability, or platform qualification.

evidence.proves: One admitted ordinary-Haxe slice verifies exact package receipts, hashes real source bytes, decodes pack and UI schemas, resolves a real map, and constructs one unpublished generation through strict generated C.
evidence.doesNotProve: General Haxe lowering, arbitrary package compatibility, live renderer publication, public ABI stability, or platform qualification.

evidence.proves: The fast Eval owner proves failed-load invariance, successful replacement, retained retired views, and exact stale/duplicate rejection; the paired runtime-content-generation tracer carries that owner through haxe.c, strict generated C, and a native observer without compiling the package graph twice.
evidence.doesNotProve: General Haxe lowering, renderer String interop, arbitrary hot reload, public ABI stability, or platform qualification.

semanticOwners: compiler frontend, HxcIR, lowering, representation, and generated-project planning

lastObserved.evidence: haxe_c-xge.20.4.4.3: test:caxecraft-package-zip-export passes complete deterministic package export and isolated handoff through the admitted Bytes/String/Array/class/enum slice on Eval and strict native C with sanitizers.

residualRisks: General Haxe-to-C remains unsupported in the capability manifest.
The official Haxe suite adapter remains readiness-only under haxe_c-6k7.

surfaces.name: C ABI, native/metal, and foreign-function behavior
protectedClaims: Typed direct-C imports and native fixture ABIs are proven only for their declared headers and consumers.
Independent native C or C++ evidence does not create a generated public ABI claim.
oracles: Independent C header/layout contracts and strict target compiler diagnostics
Hand-authored C and C++ consumers rather than generated expectations from haxe.c

evidence.proves: The bounded direct-import fixture crosses an independently authored C ABI boundary.
evidence.doesNotProve: Bindgen, arbitrary C or C++ consumption, generated exports, or ABI stability.

evidence.proves: Public ABI, bindgen, and C export remain explicit unsupported gates.
evidence.doesNotProve: Any future ABI layout or compatibility promise.

evidence.proves: The atomic runtime-content tracer crosses the typed confined POSIX package adapter and primary strict native compiler before observing real bytes, one complete generation, and successful complete-owner publication.
evidence.doesNotProve: A public C ABI, arbitrary foreign functions, Windows package IO, another platform tuple, or compiler conformance.

evidence.proves: An independent C consumer observes the Haxe-authored directory package tracer while the typed POSIX boundary supplies the real bytes.
evidence.doesNotProve: A generated public API, arbitrary C interop, ZIP support, Windows package IO, ABI stability, or platform qualification.

evidence.proves: An independent C consumer observes the Haxe-authored complete ZIP exporter and reader after the typed POSIX boundary supplies every real package payload; an isolated rerun uses the already-built consumer beside only the archive.
evidence.doesNotProve: A generated public API, arbitrary C interop, Windows package IO, ABI stability, another compiler family, or platform qualification.

semanticOwners: typed c.* contracts, imports, generated headers, native consumers, and build adapters

lastObserved.evidence: haxe_c-xge.20.4.4.3: a strict native C consumer observes complete package ZIP export and isolated reload through the typed POSIX file boundary; the capability manifest still marks public-c-abi unsupported.

residualRisks: No generated public header, ABI manifest, or compatibility policy exists.
Native fixture success cannot advance compiler conformance or platform support.

surfaces.name: Runtime, memory, ownership, and lifetime behavior
protectedClaims: Runtime and memory claims require generated native execution and the applicable sanitizer or failure-path observer.
A generated-C snapshot or semantic pass cannot substitute for ownership and lifetime execution.
oracles: Pinned Haxe Eval behavior for shared semantics
ASan and UBSan for invalid memory and undefined C behavior
Independent allocator and C consumer invariants

evidence.proves: The declared collector seed has a native and sanitizer owner.
evidence.doesNotProve: Complete object-graph, thread-root, finalization, or platform collector support.

evidence.proves: String runtime behavior, including fresh enum-payload projection and retained aggregate aliases, is compared with an independent Haxe oracle and native sanitizer observers.
evidence.doesNotProve: Other managed callback payload types, a complete runtime, leak detection on hosts without LeakSanitizer, or platform qualification.

evidence.proves: Borrowed and fresh Bytes owners cross compiler-generated switch and conditional joins with exactly one selected owner; explicit nullable locals distinguish absence from an empty allocation and retain valid aliases across checked unwrap, replacement, early-return cleanup, and return transfer under strict native execution and the eligible sanitizers.
evidence.doesNotProve: Nullable Bytes parameters, returns, fields, or other erased-null storage shapes; a complete runtime; unrelated managed carrier types; leak detection where unavailable; a stable ABI; or platform qualification.

evidence.proves: The bounded JSON tree and rejection paths complete real generated native cleanup under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.
evidence.doesNotProve: A complete runtime, leak detection where unavailable, arbitrary pack loading, compiler conformance, or another platform.

evidence.proves: All positive and rejected package candidates complete under generated native execution and the runner's eligible sanitizer observers.
evidence.doesNotProve: A complete runtime, leak detection where unavailable, arbitrary mods, ZIP parsing, concurrent package activation, or another platform.

evidence.proves: The frozen copied archive, indexed entry owners, independent read results, and 36 rejected archive candidates complete under generated native execution and the eligible AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer observers.
evidence.doesNotProve: A complete runtime, streaming or compressed archives, leak detection where unavailable, concurrent package activation, arbitrary mod safety, or another platform.

evidence.proves: All complete-package payload owners, two independent archive results, bounded ZIP-reader owners, negative preflight candidates, and isolated native reload complete under strict execution and the eligible AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer observers.
evidence.doesNotProve: A complete runtime, streaming or compressed archives, concurrent package activation, arbitrary mod safety, leak detection where unavailable, or another platform.

evidence.proves: Real package bytes become immutable content/UI models and complete positive and malformed-candidate cleanup under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.
evidence.doesNotProve: Publication into a live renderer, complete runtime ownership, arbitrary pack safety, semantic conformance outside this admitted slice, or another platform.

evidence.proves: Real receipt, pack, UI, and map bytes remain private until one coherent generation is built under native AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer observers; Eval owns exact malformed, stale, mismatched, unlisted, and missing coordinator outcomes, while native schema and level owners retain malformed cleanup evidence.
evidence.doesNotProve: Native execution of every coordinator rejection permutation, live generation replacement, a complete runtime, leak detection where unavailable, arbitrary package safety, or another platform.

evidence.proves: The complete owner retains one coherent registry, catalog, level/session, and receipt snapshot; Eval proves successful replacement plus failed-load, stale, duplicate, and retired-alias invariance, while the paired strict native tracer publishes a separately rebuilt session from one real verified package and retains both graphs under sanitizers.
evidence.doesNotProve: Concurrent publication, native execution of every rejection permutation, renderer integration, a complete runtime, leak detection where unavailable, or another platform.

semanticOwners: runtime feature planning, allocator/collector slices, managed values, cleanup, and sanitizer lanes

lastObserved.evidence: haxe_c-xge.20.4.4.3: the complete 9.5 MB package ZIP export, two-result ownership, reader round trip, negative preflight paths, and isolated reload pass strict native execution and ASan/UBSan on the local Clang host.

residualRisks: The hxrt implementation remains a bounded collection of admitted slices, not a complete runtime.
Sanitizer success on one host cannot qualify other platforms or prove Haxe semantic conformance.

evidence.proves: Current hosted jobs exercise selected compilers, native builds, and platform probes.

semanticOwners: toolchain pins, platform facts, strict native builds, compiler families, sanitizers, and build consumers
